segments.title: 第185章 失戀
segments.content:
Chapter 185: Lovelorn

Changning City, Wenyue Group.

Urban genre editorial team.

Qian Zhou was currently sitting in his office chair, his face beaming with high spirits.

He kept refreshing the page on his computer, staring at the data displayed on the backend. He had been doing this for the entire day.

Aside from replying to some authors' messages, going to the restroom, and eating, he had been almost constantly watching the growth trends of various stats for "I'm Really Not a Star."

He was so excited, not just because he had his first book with ten thousand average subscriptions under his belt.

It was also because, judging by the current trend, the future potential that "I'm Really Not a Star" could unleash and the heights it could reach were far beyond what a mere ten thousand subscriptions could summarize.

If the traffic conversion rate this time was high enough, then Chong Ran's book might have a chance to shoot for twenty thousand average subscriptions in one go, or maybe even higher.

Unfortunately, "I'm Really Not a Star" had only just launched today on Wenyue Group's other partner platforms, and Qian Zhou would have to wait until next month to get the data from those channels.

He had no idea how "I'm Really Not a Star" was performing on the various partner sites.

Logically, a simple, satisfying novel like the one Chong Ran wrote should also be very popular on the partner sites.

But until he got the data from those channels, Qian Zhou couldn't be at ease for even a day, and his heart kept itching.

Even so, just the performance of "I'm Really Not a Star" on the main site today was enough for Qian Zhou to cheer and celebrate.

From just after two in the morning until five in the evening now, "I'm Really Not a Star" had been sitting firmly on the throne of the number one spot on the entire site's bestseller chart, unshakeable.

On one hand, this was because the traffic drawn by this event was indeed massive. On the other hand, Chong Ran had been more than pulling his weight.

At a rate of one new chapter every half an hour, he had already updated over thirty chapters so far!

A total of sixty to seventy thousand characters!

This update volume not only shocked the readers of "I'm Really Not a Star" but also spread like wildfire across major reader QQ groups and various forums and Tieba threads.

As a result, even readers who didn't usually pay attention to reading events were passively made aware of the book "I'm Really Not a Star."

While shocked by the huge update volume, they also came over to join the fun out of curiosity.

Consequently, the traffic directed to "I'm Really Not a Star" snowballed. Instead of gradually declining as the event went on, it showed a trend of intensifying.

Especially since today was January 1st, the day for deciding the top spots on the monthly recommendation ticket and monthly ticket charts. Chong Ran, with the traffic from the event and the overwhelming number of updates, had naturally secured the top position on the monthly ticket chart.

With the bonus of being number one on both charts, any reader who followed Qidian would basically be unable to avoid this book when looking for something to read.

Of course, this didn't mean that Chong Ran's book was truly number one on the entire site.

His current achievement was purely the result of a massive surge of traffic.

Once this wave of hype passed, it would still come down to solid strength.

But for Qian Zhou, even if he only had Chong Ran's book under his wing, it was already enough to guarantee his performance ranked among the top editors.

At the very least, he wouldn't be eliminated for being at the bottom.

In contrast, the female editor next to Qian Zhou named Qing Yue had not been having an easy time recently.

With the gradual decline of Hallyu novels during this period, her previous advantage in author resources had instead become a burden, affecting the performance of the books she signed.

After all, a large number of her authors had started out writing Hallyu novels. When this category of books slowly became unpopular, it became especially difficult for these authors to transition.

After multiple failures, most authors, disheartened, might have no choice but to go back to regular jobs, leaving the field of web novels in disappointment.

Originally, this wasn't a big deal. After all, shifts in the trends of such small subgenres in the web novel field often happened in just a few years, or even a few months.

Besides, Qing Yue herself was not a senior editor. It was perfectly normal for a situation like this to occur.

Editors in other genres would occasionally encounter similar situations.

But what Qing Yue found a bit unbearable was that the newbie next to her, who had arrived several months after her, had produced several boutique-level books in just half a year.

And that was fine.

Even producing a book with ten thousand average subscriptions would have been whatever.

But no one could have expected that Qian Zhou would manage to get a weirdo book like "I'm Really Not a Star."

Under Qidian's normal recommendation process, this book had only shown the performance of a regular boutique-level novel.

But just because the author wrote an original song that was lucky enough to be sold as the theme song for a TV series.

And was lucky enough to have its decent melody highlighted by that trashy series.

Then was extremely lucky to get in touch with the song's singer and do a joint interview event.

With a combo like that, she felt that if you had swapped it for any of the boutique-level Hallyu novels under her, they would have taken off just the same.

The more she thought about it, the more annoyed she became.

But Qian Zhou didn't care. He would even post backend screenshots in their editors' work group from time to time, reporting one success after another.

"It's a shame it was a bit late," Hong Dou, the chief editor of the Urban team, said regretfully. "If Chong Ran had written this book a few months earlier, he could have made it to our annual conference this year."

"Boss, no need to rush this," Qian Zhou said cheerfully. "Chong Ran is only 16 this year, his future is long. If he didn't make it this year, there's always next year."

"That's true," Hong Dou smiled, happy in his heart as well.

Although Chong Ran wasn't an author he had personally nurtured, as the chief editor, having a hit book like "I'm Really Not a Star" emerge from his team was also a considerable boost to his performance. It was a good thing no matter how you looked at it. But Qing Yue, who was on the side, suddenly threw cold water on the conversation, "High school students don't have much life experience to begin with. It's already great that he could write one hit book. If he can't properly settle down in the future after earning so much in royalties, it's hard to say if he'll get a big head and his next book will just fall flat."

What she said, purely from a logical standpoint, wasn't wrong.

But saying something like this to Qian Zhou, who was in high spirits, was somewhat meant to irk him.

However, Qian Zhou wasn't angry at all right now.

If it were before, he might have had such concerns.

But ever since meeting Chong Ran in person, Qian Zhou no longer had such thoughts.

Because that kid was just too mature. Whether in his conduct or his actions, he possessed a steadiness different from his peers, and there was no trace of the arrogance or conceit one might expect after making a fortune.

So, facing Qing Yue's passive-aggressive remarks, Qian Zhou just smiled it off. "He's a top student at a key high school, with grades that are among the best in his school. It's already impressive that he can find time to write web novels."

"Even if he stops writing web novels in the future, he'll at least be a top student from a 985 university."

"So I don't need to worry about these things for him. I just need to do what an editor should do."

After he said this, Qing Yue's expression changed slightly. She moved her lips but didn't know what to say, only managing to mumble a few words under her breath that no one around could hear clearly.

"Alright," Chief Editor Hong Dou glanced at Qing Yue, then stood up and said, "The annual conference is tomorrow. I have to meet a few authors for dinner tonight. If any of you have authors you know attending the conference, you can also arrange to have a meal or something."

At this point, Hong Dou added with a cheerful laugh, "These guys are all big shots, each richer than the last. We can't be too polite, so let's freeload a few more meals."

After he said that, the other two senior editors also stood up. They clearly had authors under them who had come to Changning City for the conference.

Only Qian Zhou and Qing Yue remained at the company, as they didn't have any major authors under them.

Qian Zhou paid no more attention to Qing Yue next to him, opened QQ on his computer, and found Chong Ran's profile picture.

Qian Zhou: What are you up to? Still writing?

Chong Ran: Nah, I'm at home for New Year's Day.

Qian Zhou: The thirty-plus chapters you released today, were they all from your stockpile?

Chong Ran: Of course. I'm not a god. How could I possibly write two thousand characters every half an hour without stopping?

Qian Zhou: So... how many are you planning to release today?

Chong Ran: One chapter every half hour, for a total of 49 chapters, plus an extra chapter that will be updated in the early morning today, to make it an even 50.

Qian Zhou: Freaking amazing...

Besides "freaking amazing," Qian Zhou didn't know what else to say.

This kid still had to attend classes on weekdays. How on earth did he manage to build up such a large stockpile of chapters?

A full 50 chapters!

In terms of word count, that's a whole one hundred thousand words!

Thinking of this, Qian Zhou couldn't help but open the author group he managed and sent a message.

Qian Zhou: You guys, all you do is chat in the group all day long.

Qian Zhou: Look at Chong Ran! 50 chapters in one day!

Qian Zhou: My expectations for you aren't high. Can't you just write four or five thousand words a day and not go on hiatus at the drop of a hat?

Li Luo himself was also in this group, but he usually remained a lurker.

When he saw Qian Zhou post this in the author group right after chatting with him, he couldn't help but laugh out loud.

Looks like the pressure to update had really been applied.

"What are you looking at?"

On the sofa in the living room of Apartment 401 in Jincheng Community, Ying Chanxi saw the corners of Li Luo's mouth curl up and leaned over suspiciously to ask.

But Li Luo's hands were lightning fast, and he instantly switched to the chat with Zhao Rongjun.

Zhao Rongjun: I'm lovelorn.

Li Luo: Oh? Are you sure you're lovelorn?

Zhao Rongjun: Okay, I admit, it probably doesn't count as lovelorn... Luo Jiajia really does have a boyfriend.

Ying Chanxi, who was next to him, peeked curiously for a moment and couldn't help but ask, "Zhao Rongjun has someone he likes?"

"How can you call that 'like'?" Li Luo shook his head. "It's just a boy's self-generated infatuation born from sudden preferential treatment."

As long as a girl wasn't so unattractive that she was impossible to look at, she could easily win the favor of a boy like Zhao Rongjun just by showing him a little kindness from time to time.

Most boys grew up lacking this kind of kindness from the opposite sex. The moment they encountered it, they would mistake it for love.

Li Luo: Come out tomorrow. Bro will play basketball with you.

Zhao Rongjun: Okay, but can you not bring Ying Chanxi and the others?

Li Luo: What's wrong with that?

Zhao Rongjun: It just makes me miserable to see how close you guys are now.

Li Luo: Then do you want to tell Xixi directly? She's sitting right next to me and saw everything.

Zhao Rongjun: ???

The next second.

Li Luo's phone was snatched away.

Li Luo: Don't worry, I'll come along tomorrow too. I'll comfort you properly!

(End of this chapter)
